==English== [[File:Adriaen Brouwer, Bauernrauferei beim Kartenspiel (c. 1630–1640).jpg|thumb|Fight ([[brawl]])]] ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:fighten|id=verb|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*peḱ- (pluck)}} From {{inh|en|enm|fighten||to fight}}, from {{inh|en|ang|feohtan||to fight, combat, strive}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fehtan||to fight}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fehtaną||to comb, tease, shear, struggle with}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*peḱ-||to comb, shear}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|fecht||to fight}}, {{cog|fy|fjochtsje}}, {{m|fy|fjuchte||to fight}}, {{cog|nl|vechten||to fight}}, {{cog|nds|fechten||to fight}}, {{cog|de|fechten||to fence}}, {{cog|da|fægte||to fence, to fight (using blade weapons)}}, {{cog|nb,nn|fekte||to fence}}, {{cog|sv|fäkta||to fence, to fight (using blade weapons), to wave vigorously (and carelessly) with one's arms}}, {{cog|la|pectō||comb, thrash|pos=verb}}, {{cog|sq|pjek||to hit, strive, fight}}, {{cog|grc|πέκω||comb or card wool|pos=verb}}. Related also to {{cog|ang|feht||wool, shaggy pelt, fleece}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{enPR|fīt|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/faɪt/}} * {{audio|en|En-uk-fight.ogg|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/fəɪt/|[fəɪʔ]|a=US,Canada}} * {{audio|en|En-us-fight.ogg|a=GA}} * {{IPA|en|[fʌɪt]|a=Canadian raising}} * {{IPA|en|/fɑɪt/|a=AU}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪt|s=1}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|fought,fit|+,foughten}} # {{n-g|Senses relating to physical conflict:}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To engage in combat with; to oppose physically, to contest with. ##: {{ux|en|My grandfather '''fought''' the Nazis in World War II.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To conduct or engage in (battle, warfare, a cause, etc.). ##: {{ux|en|Our soldiers '''fought''' the battle just over that hill.}} ##* {{RQ:KJV|2 Timothy|4|7|passage=I have '''fought''' a good fight.}} ##* {{RQ:KJV|book=1 Timothy|chapter=6|verse=12|passage='''Fight''' the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.}} ##* {{RQ:Addison Cato|2|text=His Suff’rings ſhine, and ſpread a Glory round him;
Greatly unfortunate, he '''fights''' the Cauſe
Of Honour, Virtue, Liberty, and ''Rome''.}} ##* {{RQ:Macaulay Johnson|passage=was left to '''fight''' his way through the world.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[contend]] in physical conflict, either singly or in war, battle, etc. ##: {{ux|en|A wounded animal will '''fight''' tooth and nail; relentless, savage and murderous.}} ## {{lb|en|reciprocal}} To [[contend]] in physical conflict with each other, either singly or in war, battle, etc. ##: {{ux|en|The two boxers have been '''fighting''' for more than half an hour.}} ## {{lb|en|causative}} To cause to fight; to manage or manoeuvre in a fight. ##: {{co|en|to '''fight''' cocks; to '''fight''' one’s ship}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[strive]] for something; to campaign or [[contend]] for success. #: {{ux|en|He '''fought''' for the Democrats in the last election.}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=7|passage=Old Applegate, in the stern, just set and looked at me, and Lord James, amidship, waved both arms and kept hollering for help. I took a couple of everlasting big strokes and managed to grab hold of the skiff's rail, close to the stern. Then, for a jiffy, I hung on and '''fought''' for breath.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2014-07-05|volume=412|issue=8894 |url=http://www.economist.com/news/books-and-arts/21606252-ideal-political-role-model-freedom-fighter|title=Freedom fighter |passage={{q-g|Edmund}} Burke continued to '''fight''' for liberty later on in life. He backed Americans in their campaign for freedom from British taxation. He supported Catholic freedoms and freer trade with Ireland, in spite of his constituents’ ire. He wanted more liberal laws on the punishment of debtors.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170114234506/http://www.economist.com:80/news/books-and-arts/21606252-ideal-political-role-model-freedom-fighter?|archivedate=14 January 2017}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[try]] to [[overpower]]; to [[fiercely]] [[counteract]]. #: {{ux|en|The government pledged to '''fight''' corruption.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of colours or other design elements: to [[clash]]; to fail to [[harmonize]]. =====Usage notes===== *The reciprocal sense of "fight" is a common elision of the phrase "fight each other", since context provides the meaning. "Each other" is commonly used with other verbs for an explicit reciprocal sense. *The reciprocal sense of "fight", which refers to two entities fighting each other, contrasts with the reflexive sense of the word "infight", which refers to entities of a group fighting each other. =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|old=1|past=fought|past_2sg_old=foughtest|past_ptc_old=foughten}} =====Synonyms===== *
